transcript:
Header: 2026-08-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: 54m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendez (NovaMed Head of AI), Aisha Patel (Clinical Data Lead), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Lena Brooks (Compliance)

Summary: (auto) High-level plan for quality evaluation POC: golden prompts, regression harness, hallucination checks, scoring thresholds, dataset sizing and timeline for two benchmark runs.

Topics: success criteria; workload sizing; benchmarks & metrics; golden prompts & test sets; regression testing cadence; hallucination/format checks; scoring approach; timelines and responsibilities.

00:00:06 Jordan: yeah, hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, we have Priya and Miguel with me, we wanna cover the eval plan today and make sure we're aligned on what success looks like for the POC.
00:00:22 Carlos: thanks Jordan, excited. Quick background — we're doing automated clinical note summarization for discharge summaries, primary constraints are PHI removal, accuracy on medication lists, and zero critical hallucinations. Our pilot scope is central region hospitals, about 20k notes/month.
00:00:39 Priya: got it — so for the POC we'd propose a focused quality eval plan: 1) golden prompt set representing typical note types, 2) regression harness to run nightly/after-commit checks, 3) hallucination detection rules + format validation, 4) scoring with both automatic metrics and human-in-the-loop spot checks.
00:00:58 Aisha: can you be more specific on the metrics? we use clinical accuracy not just ROUGE.
00:01:05 Priya: yes — our baseline scoring: ROUGE-L for overall overlap, entity-level F1 for medications, diagnoses and procedures, and a hallucination score that flags any medically implausible statements. We'll also include a "safety fail" threshold — e.g. if any hallucinated medication appears in a summary it's an immediate fail for that sample.
00:01:27 Lena: that safety threshold is critical for compliance. Also need to know data residency and auditability for all eval outputs.
00:01:35 Miguel: on the audit side we can provide per-request logs, model versioning, and encrypted artifacts. We'll share SOC2 artifacts in the repo — I'll follow up.
00:01:45 Tom: timeline? we have a board review mid-September so need measurable results earlier.
00:01:50 Jordan: understood — propose 6-week POC: week 0 onboarding + dataset prep, week 1 first benchmark run on a 500-note seed set, weeks 2-4 iterative tuning + nightly regression, week 5 second benchmark (2k notes) and qualitative review, week 6 final report + recommendations. So that fits mid-September target.
00:02:13 Carlos: sounds reasonable. For dataset size, we plan to provide 500 seed notes, then expand to 2k for the larger benchmark. Are those numbers sufficient?
00:02:21 Priya: yes for initial signal — 500 gives us enough variance for preliminary scoring; 2k gives statistical power for entity-level F1 on meds/diagnoses. If you have specific bucket distributions (ICU vs ER vs ambulatory) share them and we'll stratify sampling.
00:02:40 Aisha: note formats vary a lot, some older notes have weird templates. How will Redwood handle format checks?
00:02:47 Priya: we'll include format validation step in the harness: check for expected sections, normalize headers, and flag malformed notes. We'll also run a pre-processing sanitization step to ensure PII is removed — but you also must deidentify before sharing.
00:03:04 Carlos: about hallucination detection — can you explain the approach?
00:03:09 Priya: mix of heuristics and model-based checks. Heuristics: medication name mismatch, improbable dosages, new meds not in the input note. Model-based: a secondary verifier model that scores faithfulness. We'll combine signals into a hallucination score and threshold for fails.
00:03:28 Tom: will the verifier be an external call or run locally in our private deployment?
00:03:33 Miguel: for the POC we can run on Redwood Hosted but for private deployments we support VPC/private runtime. We'll capture logs and model versions either way.
00:03:44 Carlos: what's the cadence for regression tests? we want nightly and on each model change.
00:03:49 Priya: recommended: nightly batch over the golden set (25-50 golden prompts + 500 seed samples) and full-run after any model/param change. Results posted to the shared dashboard and CSV artifacts dropped in the S3 bucket.
00:04:05 Jordan: scoring approach — numeric and qualitative. Numeric: ROUGE-L, BLEU (optional), entity F1s, hallucination rate, length deviation. Qualitative: human rater spot checks on a random 5% sample focusing on safety-critical items. We'll produce a composite score and a pass/fail matrix tied to your success criteria.
00:04:28 Carlos: what's a realistic success threshold? we were thinking entity-F1 meds > 0.88 and hallucination rate < 1% on critical items.
00:04:36 Priya: that is reasonable for POC targets. For final production we'd tune thresholds per site. For the POC let's set: ROUGE-L > 0.42, meds F1 > 0.88, hallucination critical-fail rate < 1% across the 2k run.
00:04:56 Aisha: how will you generate golden prompts? we need examples across note types.
00:05:01 Priya: we'll create 25 golden prompts representing discharge, progress, consults, and ER notes. Each prompt has expected answer variants and strict checks for medication/dose/diagnosis fields. We'll send the initial set by 2026-08-14 and iterate with your SMEs.
00:05:19 Lena: compliance — can we get per-sample audit logs and the ability to redact the outputs after the POC?
00:05:25 Miguel: yes, audit logs and data retention policies are configurable; we support deletion requests and KMS-managed encryption. I'll attach the compliance packet.
00:05:36 Tom: will you run quant/throughput benchmarks too? latency matters for our near-real-time use cases.
00:05:41 Priya: for the POC we can run throughput/latency on a sample workload (avg note length ~1.2k tokens). We'll include p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1000-tokens estimates. If you want, we can run on both Hosted and Dedicated configs to show tradeoffs.
00:06:00 Carlos: cost vs latency tradeoff will be key for execs. show us ballpark numbers.
00:06:05 Jordan: we will include a cost delta table — quantized model variant vs full float, hosted vs dedicated, with expected p95 latency and per-request cost.
00:06:13 Carlos: ok. Any blockers?
00:06:16 Priya: main blocker is dataset delivery + IAM access. Also need to confirm which model family you want us to start with — open Llama-style or a Redwood-curated FP32 variant.
00:06:28 Carlos: start with the curated open model first and we'll evaluate others.
00:06:32 Jordan: great. Quick recap — deliverables: Redwood shares eval harness + golden prompts, customer shares 500 notes and S3 access, first benchmark w/ 500 notes week of 8/24, nightly regression on golden set, second benchmark w/2k notes week 9/14, final report week of 9/21. Action owners noted.
00:06:56 Aisha: one question — how do you ensure the regression harness avoids false positives for hallucination flags? our clinical reviewers get annoyed with too many false alarms.
00:07:05 Priya: we'll tune the verifier threshold on the seed 500 set with your SMEs and run an initial human review loop to calibrate. We'll aim to keep false positive rate < 5% on flagged items after calibration.
00:07:19 Lena: please include retention and encryption details in the packet.
00:07:23 Miguel: noted, will share.
00:07:28 Tom: ok let's move to sign-offs.
00:07:31 Jordan: great — thanks everyone. We'll send SOW, eval template, and golden prompts by Friday. Any other questions?
00:07:40 Carlos: none, thanks.
